properties.description: The two absences are told apart, and neither is invented: an OpenCode project reports no_hook_for_this_harness with an advisory that asks for nothing to be installed; a Claude project with no hook still reports absent; a project that never named a harness reports absent rather than impossible; and a hook the user wired themselves wins over the recorded harness, so a working nudge is never called unreachable. 7 cases in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs (19 in the module, 190 in the crate, all passing).
properties.findings: ALSO DEMONSTRATED LIVE against real projects with the rebuilt binary — loop_status returned {"no_hook_for_this_harness":{"harnesses":"opencode"}} for an OpenCode project and "absent" for one that never said. THAT LIVE RUN EARNED ITS KEEP: the unit tests passed while target/debug/reflow2-mcp was still the previous build, so `cargo test --lib` was proving the library and not the binary a user runs — rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object, caught on the day it was enforced.
properties.name: The two kinds of absent nudge are told apart, and neither is invented
